verdict: DIRECTED CHAIN (directed_chain.py): put ARROWS on the edges and follow DIRECTED chains, to beat the small-world collapse of undirected PPI. Directed layer = SIGNOR signed signaling + TRRUST (avg out-degree 14.3). Only 24% of knockouts are directed sources (have outgoing arrows) -- the rest have NO directed edge to propagate. On those that do: directed discrimination stays 2.69x at 2 hops and 1.71x at 3 hops (vs undirected's collapse to 1.0x) -- so DIRECTION DOES restore specificity: a directed cascade does not fan out to the whole cell. BUT only 40% of a knockout's movers are directionally reachable at all, and directed-closeness recall is 0.016 vs tide 0.226. So the concept is VALIDATED -- arrows fix the fan-out problem -- but the directed edges we have (SIGNOR/TRRUST, canonical) are too SPARSE to cover the response: most knockouts aren't even sources, and most movers are never reached. The bottleneck moves from 'undirected explosion' to 'directed-edge coverage'. The user's assembly-order idea is exactly the right KIND of data (it would add directed edges), but assembly order isn't in any database at scale; the scalable path to a dense DIRECTED interactome is a time-course readout (order genes by when they move) + kinase-substrate/SIGNOR-style directed edges. Deterministic.
